heuristics.extrapolation: van Oorschot-Wiener 1999, the common generic-track premise, the priced hazard sensitivity of proof Section 6.1 (-0.5*log2(1-eps) bits for a hazard deficit eps), reduced-scale 32-bit-window birthday counts on 2^20 inputs in three input families, plus exact-program consistency checks against scalar SHA3-256-r6.
heuristics.limitations: Experiments do not reach birthday scale; circuit, memory and comparator-F arithmetic do not depend on H1.
heuristics.scope: The fixed r6 row-pair chain g of proof Section 2, 93000 trails, exact DP threshold, replay cap, 256 lanes and at most 256*Tb evaluations.
heuristics.statement: H1 is one premise. Let A_g be this bounded attempt on the fixed deterministic walk g. In the real algorithm's probability space, only the fresh uniform word r is random. Let F be a uniformly random function on 256-bit values, independent of r, and let P_F = Pr_(r,F)[A_F succeeds] for the same attempt with each g evaluation replaced by lazy sampling from F. H1 asserts only the aggregate comparison Pr_r[A_g succeeds] >= P_F. Appendix A proves P_F >= 0.39. The following clauses are properties of comparator F used by that proof, not additional premises about g: outputs at distinct fresh inputs are uniform and independent; its iterates have the random-mapping first-collision law; a fresh output satisfies the exact distinguished-point predicate with its stated probability independently of prior collision bookkeeping; and after any lazy-sampling history, a fresh input maps to any fixed earlier output with probability 2^-256. H1 assigns no per-history conditional probability to deterministic g because the history determines r and hence all later g outputs. The aggregate success comparison is the only heuristic step.

heuristics.scope: The register file used by the straight-line program and the search; it affects the time and memory ledgers only, not the success bound.
heuristics.statement: Machine convention: the 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5 with a declared file of 1943 registers of 256 bits (1932 used by the straight line; the search state begins at register 1932; handler temporaries reuse dead straight-line registers above 255). An operation on register operands costs one word operation, with no load or store; every load and store of the other code is a charged word operation (proof Sections 3.1 and 4). The 62176 bytes of the file are counted as memory. The cost model fixes no register count.

heuristics.extrapolation: None statistical: a declared convention. Executed checks parse both encodings in software to validate the program and measured byte counts.
heuristics.limitations: A requirement of 32 bytes per straight-line instruction would add code memory; the success argument is unaffected.
heuristics.scope: The code rows of the memory ledger; it does not affect the success bound.
heuristics.statement: Code-memory charging convention: a declared encoding, since the cost model and the target profile fix none. The straight line and prefilter are stored in the two-address encoding of proof Section 3.1 (91106 bytes measured); the other code is stored in 1016 8-byte instruction words followed by 12 literal words of 32 bytes (8512 bytes measured). The encoding determines the code bytes counted in memory.

restrictions: Two distinct 128-byte one-block messages for sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1 under the injective row-pair embedding of proof Section 2 (lanes 0..3 and 10..13 carry the point, lanes 4 and 14 the pivot lane P(u)).

The bit-sliced straight line has 25439 register operations (18724 XOR, 3031 AND, 2993 OR, 691 NOT), is stored in 91057 bytes under H_code, and has SHA-256 c2d52e3ed730f2bc8e7acdaa80fd05fd246ff5aadc20de6faeb9939450a38847.
The separate prefilter has 15 OR operations, 49 encoded bytes, destination register 1936 and SHA-256 88ad15d4b5a89d38385fdb42179b15636e53cafe9cc5ed670c5a56b5bb849543.
The chained-chi table has 1,024 entries, checksum c8fa4bd9170966dc; the Python emitter verifies every entry against all 32 row inputs before use.

The assembled other code has 1016 8-byte instruction words, 12 32-byte literals, 8512 bytes and SHA-256 c656b0c5f89238d20788f98274790cf0f755a6ff7ce11addd55bb08ec762fb5e; the experiment executes it, checks eval_f against scalar SHA3-256-r6 and checks the all-no-DP limit halt.
Machine conventions H_reg and H_code (role supporting; proof Section 3.1) are those of the incumbent package with this package's measured counts.
The table has 18600 words and 93000 positional 51-bit slots; every packed-field boundary is exercised.

Appendix A and the experiment certify P_F >= 0.39 for the comparator function; success for the fixed chain g rests on H1. Exact N=33893102225923899353969877205805498318795, C=1626, memory=935025 bytes, preprocessing bound=1153085472499881472 word operations.
